messages:
alex: Heads-up — we've seen a burst of KV-cache-related OOMs on hostpool-12 over the last 3 hours. Pattern looks different from usual fragmentation: memory climbs steadily with very long contexts then spikes and OOMs during pagewalk.

maria: Logs? repro steps? any recent kernel-selection or batching changes rolled to that pool? :eyes:

alex: Pasted the snippet from the agent logs:

alex: ```
2026-03-18T14:02:11Z runtime WARNING: kv_cache: pagewalker took 4289ms for request 0x7f3a - mem_before=54.3GB mem_after=60.1GB - alloc failed: OOM
stack: runtime::kv::PageWalker::walk+0x1f3
...
```

alex: No config changes to kernel selection in that rollout window, but we did flip batching heuristic alpha->beta yesterday for low-latency paths.

daniel: Repro summary from a dev run: long multi-turn chat (avg seq 12k tokens), mixed small/huge requests (prefix reuse is high). When prefix reuse misses spike, pagewalker scans many slab segments -> thrash + compaction attempts -> steady mem growth then allocation fail.

maria: That matches a hypothesis: pagewalker doing eager full-walk and triggering background compaction which allocates more temporary structures. Could be our compaction policy is too aggressive for long-context mixes.

sasha: Quick idea: introduce a backoff on pagewalker depth for requests flagged as "long-dialog" and fall back to streaming KV eviction rather than full compaction. Term it pagewalker_backoff. We tried a sim in staging and it reduced peak transient allocation by ~30%.

alex: Can you paste the staging flags? We can do a very narrow canary on a small pool.

sasha: Sure — staging flag set:

```
pagewalker_backoff.enabled=true
pagewalker_backoff.depth_multiplier=0.6
pagewalker_backoff.alloc_budget_bytes=268435456  # 256MB
preemptive_compact.enabled=true
preemptive_compact.threshold_ms=1000
```

daniel: Also increased batching max_batch_size from 64->48 for that pool to reduce concurrency of pagewalks — cpu slightly higher, p50 latency +8ms but p99 improved since fewer OOM retries.

infra-bot: alert: OOM spike detected on hostpool-12 (count=17 in 3h). Linked incidents: INC-2026-0318-44. Canary flag rollout recommended.

maria: Sounds reasonable. What are the downsides? More CPU and potential regressed throughput for heavy short requests.

sasha: Right. In staging we saw CPU +12% on the node but 40% fewer retries and no OOMs in long-run tests. For hosted users this trades a small cost for availability. We should pair with an automatic degrade: if pagewalker_backoff prevents compaction but memory still rising, fall back to model-variant with smaller KV footprint (quantized) or reject largest requests with 429-like signal.

alex: Plan proposal:
1) Canary enable pagewalker_backoff on hostpool-12 (5% of traffic) with depth_multiplier=0.6 and alloc_budget=256MB.
2) Reduce max_batch_size to 48 on same canary.
3) Enable telemetry: kv.pagewalk.duration, kv.temp_alloc.bytes, kv.compaction.attempts, kv.fallbacks.count.
4) 2h observation window then widen if stable.

maria: Add a short-term mitigation: enable preemptive_compact.enabled=false on affected hosts to avoid compaction allocations until canary proves safe.

sasha: Implementing flags now. Patching agent to report kv.temp_alloc.bytes in telemetry (PR in flight). Rolling to 5%.

alex: After 30m into canary: so far 0 OOMs, kv.temp_alloc.bytes down ~35%, p99 latency is stable. Will hold for 2h and then decide next step. :thumbsup:

daniel: For longer-term: a) adaptive compaction (budget + reuse heuristic) b) prefer reuse over compaction when slab fragmentation low-high mix detected c) better eviction heuristics for long-contexts (LRU window tuned by seq-length). I'll draft RFC.

maria: Agreed. Also add a graceful-degrade path: when host signals high-memory and pagewalker backoff active, runtime should stream partial KV (best-effort) and include a header: X-Redwood-KV-Partial: true so clients/evals can detect degraded output.

alex: Thanks all. Owners: sasha (hotfix canary rollout), daniel (RFC for adaptive compaction), maria (observability metrics + degrade header). I'll update INC-2026-0318-44 with plan and mark P1->monitoring.
